screen5-a1.description: the word "Settings" at the top of the Settings page, beside the back chevron
screen5-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Settings"; resource_id tv_title; not used in the verdict
screen5-a1.initial_rationale: the only text is the page name, which reads as a heading; if it is a control, nothing says what pressing it does

test_cases.action: tap the word "Settings" once and wait (reading 1: it is only a heading and nothing happens)
test_cases.confirms_if: it performs an action the word "Settings" does not predict
test_cases.overturns_if: nothing happens (it is a heading, not a control) — which would make it a detection false positive rather than a purpose issue
test_cases.observed_result: after a single tap on the word, the Settings page closed and the home screen returned — the title acts as a back control (repeated twice with the same result)

screen5-a1.deciding_evidence: the title is a real control that navigates back, and nothing visible — the word "Settings" least of all — says so
screen5-a1.recommendation: make only the back chevron navigate back and stop the title from reacting to taps, or if the title bar must stay tappable, make it visibly part of the back control (e.g. "< Back")

screen5-a2.description: chevron pointing left, top-left of the Settings page
screen5-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_left; no label; not used in the verdict
screen5-a2.convention_relied_on: left chevron = back, established convention — my reading, confidence high
screen5-a2.initial_rationale: unlabeled back chevron — common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test

test_cases.confirms_if: it does something other than go back
test_cases.observed_result: the Settings page closed and the home screen returned

screen5-a2.deciding_evidence: the chevron went back, as the back convention promises

screen5-a3.description: orange banner with a crown, "Upgrade to Premium" and a right chevron
screen5-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label repeats the visible words; not used in the verdict

screen5-a3.deciding_evidence: the words say it leads to upgrading to the paid plan (not tested: judged Clear on its visible text, and tapping it would start a purchase/billing flow or change a setting)

screen5-a7.description: settings row "Add widget" with a card glyph and a chevron
screen5-a7.location: fourth row of the first card
screen5-a7.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label repeats the visible words; not used in the verdict
screen5-a7.initial_rationale: "widget" is platform jargon and the row does not say which widget or where it will be added

test_cases.action: tap "Add widget" (reading: add a PDF Reader widget to the home screen); dismiss without adding
test_cases.expected_result: a home-screen widget offer appears that shows what the widget is
test_cases.confirms_if: it opens something unrelated, or adds something without showing what
test_cases.overturns_if: the result shows and explains the widget before anything is added
test_cases.observed_result: a sheet titled "Add widget" opened showing a preview (search bar plus Home / Recent / Bookmarks / Edit PDF shortcuts), the caption "PDF Tools — One-tap access to common features", page dots for other widgets, and an "Add" button; dismissed with Back, nothing added

screen5-a7.deciding_evidence: the row opened a titled sheet that previews the widget and explains it before anything is added — what the words promised, with the jargon resolved on the next step
